label: prf:su2-emergence-volume-determinant
title: Proof: volume constraint forces $\det(g_V) = 1$
html:
Proof. Proof: volume constraint forces \det(g_V) = 1

Proof. The gauge group G is defined via Tannaka--Krein duality as the group scheme of tensor-preserving natural automorphisms of the fibre functor \tau. An element g \in G assigns an invertible linear map g_X \colon \tau(X) \to \tau(X) to every object X \in \mathbf{C}.

Because g is a natural transformation, it commutes with all morphisms in \mathbf{C}, including the volume constraint \epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \to \mathbf{1} volume constraint. Applying \tau yields the commutative diagram of R-modules

\begin{equation}\label{eq:su2-emergence-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3.5em]
  \Lambda^2 \tau(V)
    \ar[r, "\Lambda^2 g_V"]
    \ar[d, "\tau(\epsilon)"']
  & \Lambda^2 \tau(V)
    \ar[d, "\tau(\epsilon)"]
  \\
  \tau(\mathbf{1})
    \ar[r, "g_{\mathbf{1}} = \mathrm{id}"']
  & \tau(\mathbf{1})
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}

The volume constraint requires a non-degenerate epimorphism \epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \to \mathbf{1}, which forces \mathrm{rank}(V) = 2: the epimorphism is non-degenerate only when \Lambda^2 V has rank 1, and \mathrm{rank}(\Lambda^2 V) = \binom{r}{2} equals 1 precisely for r = 2 (see the fundamental object). Thus \tau(V) is a rank-2 free R-module and \Lambda^2 \tau(V) has rank 1. The induced operator \Lambda^2 g_V acts on this rank-1 module as scalar multiplication by \det(g_V). Following diagram above from the top-left to the bottom-right:

  \tau(\epsilon) \circ \Lambda^2 g_V
  =
  g_{\mathbf{1}} \circ \tau(\epsilon)
  =
  \tau(\epsilon).

Since \tau(\epsilon) is non-degenerate (hence non-zero), this forces

\begin{equation}\label{eq:det-one}
  \det(g_V) =  1,
\end{equation}

restricting the natural automorphisms from \mathrm{GL}(2) to the special subgroup \mathrm{SL}(2). \square
